headline: EU finalises streamlined ESRS standards as national EUDR enforcement rules advance
summary: The EU has finalized streamlined ESRS standards, aiding your CSRD preparations for financial year 2027. Meanwhile, Member States are advancing severe national EUDR penalties and setting new customs codes. Additionally, generic green claims bans are now active, and proposals to expand CBAM to downstream finished goods are moving towards trilogue discussions.

items.title: EU finalises streamlined ESRS and voluntary reporting standards
items.what: The EU finalised streamlined European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) alongside a new voluntary reporting standard for non-listed entities.
items.meaning: As a listed brand in CSRD scope for FY2027, the streamlined standards reduce reporting complexity and help structure ESG data requests to Chinese suppliers.
items.action: Align supplier sustainability data collection processes with the finalized ESRS framework.

items.title: Germany and Ireland introduce severe EUDR administrative rules and penalties
items.what: Germany approved rules proposing turnover-linked fines and prison sentences for severe EUDR breaches, while Ireland proposed €10m fines. Brussels also set new customs codes.
items.meaning: If tool packaging or wooden accessories fall under EUDR, non-compliance carries severe financial and criminal enforcement risks at national level.
items.action: Verify tool packaging materials and wooden components against new EUDR customs codes.

items.title: EU ban on unverified greenwashing claims comes into force
items.what: EU rules prohibiting generic and misleading environmental claims under the Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive have taken effect.
items.meaning: Consumer marketing for power tools and battery platforms sold in the EU must now be backed by strict, verifiable evidence.
items.action: Audit product packaging, battery platform marketing, and consumer-facing claims for compliance.

items.title: Italy transposes Right to Repair Directive as EU issues corrigendum
items.what: Italy confirmed national transposition of the EU Right to Repair Directive effective 22 October 2026, alongside an official EU legislative corrigendum.
items.meaning: As the legal manufacturer of tools sold in Italy, product repairability and spare part provision requirements are rapidly taking effect.
items.action: Review Italian spare part availability and repair support options ahead of 22 October.

items.title: Proposed downstream CBAM extension moves toward EU trilogue negotiations
items.what: Proposed EU amendments to extend the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism to downstream finished products are advancing toward trilogue negotiations.
items.meaning: Although imported finished power tools currently avoid CBAM carbon certificate purchases, a downstream extension could bring finished goods into scope.
items.action: Monitor trilogue negotiations to evaluate prospective carbon reporting or levy impacts on imported tools.
